subject: Staged cutover: capacity transition plan and retention questions
messages:
From: Elena Rivas <elena@pinebrook.health>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@pinebrook.health
Date: Sun, 21 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Staged cutover and data retention questions

Hi Markus —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Were starting to plan a staged cutover from our staging cluster to a Redwood Dedicated GPU pool and have a few items we'd like to confirm before the kickoff: 

- Preferred region: US-East is our first choice, but we need confirmation on whether you can guarantee cross-region KV cache fallbacks.
- Autoscale windows: can we configure predictable warm-up/burst windows for regular daily peaks (08:00-10:00 EST) without incurring full reserved capacity costs?
- KV cache persistence: during cutover we want short-term retention of KV cache across instances (4–6 hours) and an option for longer retention (30 days) for debugging — what's supported?
- Data retention and logs: legal needs confirmation of retention windows for request/response logs and whether we can get a daily export for the first 30 days.

I'll attach the initial SOW draft from procurement (copied Legal) and a sample traffic profile — those should help scope the pool. Can you propose a staged schedule (staging -> canary -> prod) and highlight any blockers?

Thanks,
Elena
Product Ops, Pinebrook Health

Attachments: pinebrook-sow-v1.pdf, traffic-profile.csv

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rivas <elena@pinebrook.health>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, olga_petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Staged cutover and data retention questions

Elena —

Appreciate the details and the SOW. High level answer first, then a proposed phased plan attached.

- Region & KV cache fallbacks: we can provision the primary pool in us-east-1 and configure cross-region fallback to us-west-2. KV cache is not "replicated" synchronously across regions by default; we provide an automatic prefix-level warm-up to reduce cold starts on fallback. For true cross-region KV replication we offer a managed replication add-on — thats an extra line item in the SOW.

- Autoscale / burst windows: yes. We support reserved baseline + scheduled burst windows where you pay for a smaller reserved pool and enable burst capacity during configured windows. That lets you avoid paying for full capacity 24/7. The attached proposed-scaling-policy.md shows pricing tiers and how burst throttles work.

- KV cache persistence: short-term KV retention (4–6 hours) is supported by default via our instance-level cache TTLs. Longer retention (30 days) requires enabling our KV-archive feature (S3-backed snapshotting) so you can replay for debugging. We'll call that out in the SOW.

- Logs & retention exports: we can set a 30-day retention for request/response logs on your Dedicated account and provide a daily export to your secure S3 bucket. Legal: exports can be encrypted with customer-managed KMS.

Next steps (proposal):
1) Confirm traffic profile numbers (RPS, p95 token rates) — see capacity-matrix.xlsx (attached).
2) We propose a three-phase cutover: a) Staging warm-up (1 week) b) Canary with 5–10% real traffic (3 days) c) Gradual ramp to prod (2 weeks).
3) Kickoff call: Wed Jun 24 or Thu Jun 25 — 60 minutes — Ops, CS engineering, and Legal.

I've attached: capacity-matrix.xlsx and proposed-scaling-policy.md. Monica/Ben/Olga/Priyom: please review the schedule and confirm operational assumptions (network change windows, maintenance blackout windows).

— Markus
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity-matrix.xlsx, proposed-scaling-policy.md

Looping in high-level ops assumptions so all parties have the same expectation before Thu's call:

Assumptions (please confirm):
- Baseline reserved capacity sized for 15 RPS steady-state (buffer for dev spikes) with scheduled burst to 100 RPS for the 08:00-10:00 ET window.
- Warm-up strategy: progressive pod starts during off-peak the evening before a scheduled burst to pre-populate KV prefixes.
- Maintenance blackouts: no maintenance between 07:30-10:30 ET on cutover days.
- KV persistence: 6-hour TTL by default; enable KV-archive snapshots daily for the first 14 days post-cutover.
- Monitoring: we will attach an eval & regression prompt set for the first 7 days to detect quality degradation during autoscale transitions.

Open questions for Legal/Procurement:
- Will Pinebrook accept the add-on for KV-archive as a one-time setup fee + monthly storage?

Action items before Thu:
- Mark: send calendar invite + agenda
- Ben: prepare runbook checklist and escalation contacts
- Olga: confirm network egress IPs and VPC peering requirements
- Priyom: confirm MLP sizing and autoscaler thresholds in the capacity matrix
